reason: The children explain how donor, object and field make giving distinctive, with verses on results, and the third discusses fields of merit at length with sutra citations and the eight kinds of giving.
The children each give a short definition (immorality, pure morality and its divisions, the four qualities of morality) backed by a verse line, with no discussion of their own.

The first child only defines meditation-born merit, but the second explains why morality leads to higher rebirth and meditation to separation, and discusses the three bases and pure Dharma-giving with autocommentary citations.
The children analyse the seven, ten and ninety-eight divisions of the latent tendencies, giving reasons and purposes for the groupings, detailed counts and the positions of other Abhidharma systems.
The two children are one-line statements that pride falls into three types and into the two abandonment categories.

The children set out which latent tendencies are non-virtuous or unspecified and which are roots, and the third raises and answers why certain views are called unspecified, explaining the four kinds of questions.
The first child argues at length that the three times exist substantially, with scripture, reasoning and an evaluation of four Sarvastivada masters, though the other two are only verse pointers.
The children briefly list the order in which the afflictions arise and their three causes, each backed by a quotation, with no further discussion.
The children explain the synonyms for the afflictions in sutra and treatise, giving reasons for each name and grouping, raising and answering points, and citing several texts.
The first child explains the three ways the seeing-abandonments are abandoned, with an example and reasoning, while the second is a one-line statement on the meditation-abandonments.
Most children are brief definitions, but the third discusses the nature of each of the five paths at length, with autocommentary citations and the sixteen moments of the path of seeing.
The children explain how insight is cultivated on the accumulation and preparation paths, and the second discusses the features of the preparation path and when a practitioner can switch lineage.
The children are a one-line definition, a list of divisions, an etymology and a pointer elsewhere, with no discussion.
The children explain the stream-enterer, once-returner, non-returner and arhat types in detail, with reasoned proofs, raised objections and answers, and citations.
